clue.text: Contented, by 10.51 to have bloomers

parts.note: contented means glad
read as Roman numerals, 10 is IO (I and O, one and nought) and 51 is LI (L for fifty, I for one)

explanation.surface: A satisfied person, at a precise time, gets to wear their knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like old-fashioned underwear, but here it means flowers. The time 10.51 has to be read as numbers spelt in letters: 1 and 0 look like I and O, and 51 in Roman numerals is LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall garden flowers, things that bloom.

clue.text: Brochures for fliers

definitions.meaning: printed pamphlets handed out to advertise something
handbills, also with a hint of things that fly, like little leaves on the wind

explanation.definitionFit: Small printed pamphlets are brochures, and the same handouts are called flyers or fliers.

clue.text: Single out in dire mastic that is breakable

indicators.note: something breakable can be smashed and reassembled, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Picking out a nasty sealant because it cracks easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is breakable' makes the anagram of IN DIRE MASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to distinguish or pick something out from the rest.

clue.text: First man in often seen on the bottle

definitions.meaning: the batsman who starts a cricket innings
a tool fitted to a bottle top to remove the cap

explanation.surface: A cricketer who walks out to bat first is often found drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the batsman who goes in first is an opener, and a bottle opener is a gadget used on bottles.

clue.text: Man, for example, lies about

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word lies are scattered around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man, say, tells untruths here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the anagram of LIES. 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Aversion is stated violently

indicators.note: violently suggests the words is stated are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A strong dislike is expressed with force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' makes the anagram of IS STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or repugnance.

clue.text: Hot tip here wager is put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ante is a stake or wager in poker

explanation.surface: A racing tip where a bet is placed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot tip' sounds like racing advice, but it is the summit of a volcano. 'is put up' turns ANTE upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a Sicilian volcano whose summit is hot and erupting.

clue.text: Unresponsive nature of someone, being a hundred years of age

parts.note: C, for century, is a hundred years
of age means old
the suffix -ness denotes a state of being

explanation.surface: A person described as a centenarian.
explanation.walkthrough: C (century), OLD and NESS, the suffix meaning a state of being, are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness is aloofness, an unfriendly lack of warmth in a person.

clue.text: Weapon used in T S Eliot play around a kind of square

indicators.note: around means the anagrammed letters are put round the next piece
play suggests the letters T S Eliot are moved about freely

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool

explanation.surface: A dagger used as a prop in a drama by the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' makes an anagram of TSELIOT, and 'around' puts that round T. 'Play' tempts as a drama by Eliot; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger, a stabbing weapon.

clue.text: Overture to get through

definitions.meaning: an approach or advance made to someone
to succeed in a test, or go past

explanation.definitionFit: A pass is an amorous advance or approach, and to pass an exam or a narrow gap is to get through it.

clue.text: Piano recital first-class

parts.note: a recital is a concert
first-class means grand, splendid

explanation.surface: A top-notch keyboard performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the largest kind of grand piano, made for concert halls.

clue.text: Producer of films helpful to people in the theatre?

definitions.text: Producer of films helpful to people in the theatre?

parts.words: Producer of films helpful to people in the theatre
parts.note: read as a movie maker for stage folk, but the films are X-ray plates and the theatre is a hospital operating theatre

explanation.surface: A movie producer who supports actors.
explanation.definitionFit: This hospital worker takes X-ray images that surgeons in the operating room rely on.

clue.text: Do they take bread only half of the time?

definitions.text: Do they take bread only half of the time?

parts.words: Do they take bread only half of the time
parts.note: bread is slang for money; part-time sportsmen are paid only for part of their work, semi meaning half

explanation.surface: A question about people who eat bread only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi-professional players earn money from sport but only part-time.

clue.text: Being so chic will raise the tone

definitions.meaning: the musical sign that lifts a note's pitch

explanation.surface: Being stylish will make a place more refined.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp dresser is smart and stylish, and in music a sharp sign raises a note by a semitone.

clue.text: Teased about being slow-moving

indicators.note: about means the letters of teased are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mocked for being sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried.

clue.text: Wine seen in East Italy is really from the west!

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are visible inside the words East Italy

explanation.surface: A wine thought to be from eastern Italy actually comes from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'eAST Italy'. The closing remark is a wink: Asti is in Piedmont, north-west Italy, and the hidden letters run west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white Italian wine.

clue.text: Symbolic tale of legal characters changing on Circle Line?

indicators.note: the letters of legal change their positions

parts.note: the characters (letters) of legal
a circle is the shape of the letter O
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A tale of lawyers swapping places on a London Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes ALLEG from LEGAL. The Circle Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for deeper meanings.

clue.text: Bargain truck?

definitions.meaning: to negotiate a deal, buy and sell

explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell or barter, and truck is an old word for exchange, as in having no truck with someone.

clue.text: The opening to Mahler's pieces, possibly? They can lift people!

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of The
possibly signals that the letters of the composer's name, broken into pieces, are rearranged

parts.note: Gustav Mahler, the composer, with the possessive S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: The start of a Mahler composition might be uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opening' gives T; 'pieces, possibly' makes the anagram of MAHLERS, possessive S included. 'They can lift people' also hints at warm underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising columns of warm air carry gliders and birds aloft.

clue.text: Gold bags emptied of balls

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of the word bags is removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Gold bags with nothing left in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves BS, the first and last letters of 'bags'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs are spheres or globes.

clue.text: Fish left in straw hats?

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for the hats

parts.note: boaters are stiff flat straw hats

explanation.surface: A fish abandoned among summer headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat, traditional in British summer boating. 'in' puts L inside BOATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are smoked herrings.

clue.text: Envoy is a general packing a gun

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the general's name contains the gun

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A diplomat who is a military commander carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' looks like the gangster sense, carrying a weapon; here it means holding inside. Gat is old American slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a papal or official ambassador.

clue.text: Tolerance, say, in the nursery?

parts.note: two words for leeway or slack laid side by side describe a children's room for games

explanation.surface: Indulgence shown to small children.
explanation.walkthrough: Play and room both mean tolerance or leeway, as in play in a rope; together they name where children play.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's games room in a home is a nursery space.

clue.text: Capital at that time surrounded by Roman unit of weight

indicators.note: surrounded by means the word for at that time sits inside the Roman unit

parts.note: the as was an ancient Roman unit of weight and coin
at that time means then

explanation.surface: A capital city once enclosed by Roman measures.
explanation.walkthrough: The as was a Roman bronze coin and also a pound weight, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Potter's art showing G-man emphasis, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of G-man emphasis can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A ceramicist's work displays a federal agent's stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes the anagram of GMANEMPHASIS. 'Potter' is not a ceramicist but Stephen Potter, who wrote the humorous book on winning by gamesmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Potter's book described the art of winning by unsporting psychological ploys.

clue.text: China tea?

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang, china plate, for a friend
a South American herbal infusion drunk from a gourd

explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate means friend, and maté is a South American herbal drink brewed like tea.

clue.text: Average Japanese play jolly?

parts.note: No (Noh) is classical Japanese drama
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: An ordinary Japanese show that is cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual or typical standard.

clue.text: Colours for writer on Rugby, would you say?

indicators.note: would you say signals that the name is spoken, and it sounds like a different word

parts.note: Thomas Hughes wrote Tom Brown's Schooldays, set at Rugby School

explanation.surface: Team colours chosen by a sports journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby here is Rugby School, the English public school, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Hues are shades or tints.

clue.text: One who presents accounts of small shopkeeper?

definitions.meaning: a storyteller who recounts events again
a trader selling in small quantities to the public

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who keeps the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who retells a story is a re-teller, and a shopkeeper who sells goods to the public is a seller in small quantities.

clue.text: Suspicion of corrosion following vapour from condensation

indicators.note: following means the word for corrosion comes after the word for vapour

parts.note: mist forms when water vapour condenses
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A doubt arising after rust forms from damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is a lack of trust, doubt about someone.
